# Rework round 10 claims (personal_loan_servicing; renderer source scan render_r1)

R1-1 (factor effect gated through another factor): closed — the courtesy computation now defines the courtesy share itself. The standard amount is the unpaid part times courtesy_share_standard. Every courtesy point is added to the courtesy share, which is then held between zero and one. The waiver form is a separate shape choice that reads only the courtesy-waiver history: it sets the share the courtesy share starts from and any amount kept back. The order-of-steps sentence states the order once. Each point factor now changes the standard computation on its own, and the form no longer reads any point. Mechanical checks across the whole charter, on both task worlds:
- every parameter factor alone moves the all-baseline result;
- no factor binding reads another factor's binding (this check also moved the charged return's date, which two returned-fee factors read, into a shared plain binding);
- no parameter factor reaches the result only through a method factor.
R1-2 (plain bindings and single-factor quantities): closed — every plain binding in the six policies is quoted from a plain rule sentence. The waived fee's due date, used only by the return-reason point, now belongs to that factor. The remaining single-factor reads are baseline quantities used by their factor's baseline (schedule figure, schedule amount, base interest rate), so they stay plain.
R1-3 (departures from in-force base sentences): closed — the AutoPay rule now names its scope: it sets the rate only when no active hardship plan on the loan sets its own rate. On a loan whose active plan sets a rate, it restates the base content: the discount never applies on top of the plan rate, so the plan rate governs while the plan is active, and the discounted rate resumes when it ends if AutoPay is still on. The compute gives the plan rate in that case. The rule now covers a pre-plan rate equal to or above the base rate, matching the compute, and the ladder says the same.
R1-4 (a count that subtracts one): closed — the first-return count leaves out the return being charged only when that return falls in the window, so it never goes below zero. The rule says the same. This was the only count that subtracts one; the net counts compare only against positive thresholds.
R1-5 (window boundaries): closed — the first-late and first-return windows now say "fewer than 12 whole calendar months before", as within_months computes. A sweep moved every remaining "in the N whole months before" phrase in the ladders to "fewer than N whole months before", and the tier labels in both task files were relabelled to match.
R1-6 (convention sentences): closed — the shared whole-month convention sentence is gone from all six rules. Every sentence that counts whole months now carries the convention itself. Every sentence that counts days (quote window, day-rate split, hold, pay-cycle form, AutoPay restored point) carries the day-count convention. Each compute_basis quote was re-fitted to its new text.
R1-7 (wording edges): closed — the refinance amount is "rounded up to a whole dollar (an amount already in whole dollars is kept as it is)", matching the ceiling. The AutoPay rule says the borrower enrolls personally, by phone, as the enrollment tool records. The refinance rule says "personally" for the same reason.
Proof text: closed — the courtesy all-baseline figure moved (it now starts from the standard share), so task 1's computation baseline, dossier, form trace and amount tracing were rewritten. Tier labels were regenerated where ladder wording changed. A mechanical sweep is clean: tiers, factor and all-baseline results, trace labels, edge copies, dossier quotes and retired terms. Scored values are unchanged.
